﴿Creator of the heavens and the earth﴾. Its explanation has already passed (al-An'am: 14). ﴿He has made for you from yourselves mates﴾, that is, from the likes of your own creation, ﴿spouses﴾, women. ﴿And among the cattle, mates﴾, kinds, males and females. The meaning is that He created for you the male and the female among all living animals. ﴿He multiplies you through it﴾. Regarding this there are three opinions. The first: He creates you, said by al-Suddi. The second: He sustains you, said by Muqatil. The third: He increases you in number, said by al-Farra'. Regarding ﴿in it﴾ (fihi) there are two opinions.

The first: it remains in its original sense, said by most scholars. On this view, there are three opinions concerning the pronoun (ha' al-kinayah). The first: it refers to the wombs of the females, since the mates have already been mentioned, said by Zayd ibn Aslam. On this view the meaning is: He creates you in the wombs of women. Ibn Qutaybah went in this direction, saying: He creates you in the womb or in the spouse. Ibn Jarir said: He creates you through what has been made for you of your mates, and sustains you through what He has made for you of the cattle.

The second: it refers to the earth, said by Ibn Zayd. On this view the meaning is: He multiplies you through what He created of the heavens and the earth.

The third: it refers back to the act of making mentioned above. Then, regarding the meaning of the statement, there are two opinions. The first: He sustains you through what has been made of the cattle, said by Muqatil. Allah's words: ﴿And that which We revealed to you﴾, that is, from the Qur'an and the laws of Islam. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is: He prescribed that which We revealed to you, and He prescribed for you what He enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus. Allah's words: ﴿Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills﴾, that is, He selects from His servants for His religion, ﴿and guides to Himself whom He wills﴾, to His religion, ﴿those who turn back﴾, that is, who return to His obedience.

Then He mentioned their division after He had enjoined upon him the abandoning of division. He said: ﴿And they did not become divided except after knowledge had come to them﴾, meaning the People of the Book. Regarding this there are three opinions. The first: after the abundance of their knowledge, out of rebellion. The second: after they knew that division was misguidance. The third: after the Qur'an had come to them, out of rebellion against Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾ concerning the delay of the deniers of this nation until the Day of Resurrection, ﴿it would have been judged between them﴾ by sending punishment upon the deniers. ﴿And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them﴾, meaning the Jews and the Christians, ﴿after their prophets﴾, that is, after their prophets, ﴿are in doubt concerning it﴾, that is, concerning Muhammad (ﷺ).

Allah is the One who sent down the Book (ﷺ) — meaning the Qur'an — ﴿with truth﴾, i.e., He did not send it down for any purpose other than truth. ﴿And the Balance﴾: regarding this there are two views. The first is that it means justice; this is what Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and the majority said. The second is that it is that by which things are weighed; this is related from Mujahid. The meaning of its being sent down is the inspiring of creatures to act by it, and Allah's command to them to be equitable. Justice was called a balance because the balance is the instrument of equity and equalizing between creatures. The full explanation of the verse is discussed in [al-Ahzab: 63].

His saying, ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾: because they do not fear what it contains, since they do not believe in its occurrence, so they ask for its establishment out of disbelief and mockery. ﴿But those who believe are fearful of it﴾, i.e., they are apprehensive of it, ﴿because they know they will be called to account and recompensed, and they do not know what will come of them﴾. ﴿And they know that it is the truth﴾, i.e., that it will certainly occur. ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the Hour are in far-off error﴾, i.e., they argue about its occurrence, ﴿because they did not reflect, so that they would know Allah's power to establish it.

Regarding ﴿His servants﴾ here there are two views. The first is that they are the believers. The second is that it is general, covering all. His gentleness toward the wicked is that He does not destroy him.

﴿He provides for whom He wills﴾, i.e., He widens provision for him.

His saying, ﴿Whoever desires the tillage of the Hereafter﴾: Ibn Qutaybah said: i.e., the work of the Hereafter. It is said, "So-and-so cultivates the world," meaning he works for it and gathers wealth. So the meaning is: whoever intends by his deed the Hereafter ﴿We will increase for him in his tillage﴾, i.e., We will multiply his good deeds for him.

The exegetes said: whoever intends to act for Allah in a way that pleases Him, Allah will help him in His worship; and whoever desires the world, preferring it over the Hereafter because he does not believe in the Hereafter, We will give him from it, which is what was apportioned for him, ﴿and he will have no share in the Hereafter﴾, because he is a disbeliever in it and did not work for it.

(p-284) His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: I do not ask of you any reward for it﴾. Regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse there are three opinions.

The first: the polytheists used to harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Makkah, so this verse was revealed. Al-Dahhak narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: when he came to Madinah, he was afflicted with calamities and had no abundance in his hand. The Ansar said: "This man has been guided by Allah through you, and he has no abundance in his hand, so gather for him some of your wealth that will not harm you." They did so and brought it to him, and then this verse was revealed. This is also related from Ibn 'Abbas.

The third: the polytheists gathered in an assembly, and some of them said to others: "Do you think Muhammad asks a reward for what he undertakes?" Then this verse was revealed. Qatadah said this.

(p-284) The pronoun in ﴿for it﴾ refers to the guidance he brought.

Regarding the exception here there are two opinions.

The first: it is an exception from the same genus, so that it would mean he is asking a reward. Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of al-Dahhak, pointed to this meaning, then said: "This was abrogated (naskh, the cancellation of a ruling by a later revelation) by His saying: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours…﴾ [Saba: 47]." The second: it is an exception from something other than the first, because the prophets do not ask a reward for conveying their message. The meaning is: rather, I remind you of affection for the kinsfolk. A group narrated this meaning from Ibn 'Abbas, including al-Awfi. This is the choice of the verifiers (al-muhaqqiqun) and is the correct view, so abrogation does not apply at all.

The first: the meaning of the speech is: except that you love me because of my kinship with you. Ibn 'Abbas, Ikrimah and Mujahid said this, and most scholars agree. Ibn 'Abbas said: "There was no clan of the Quraysh except that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had kinship among them."

The third: the meaning is: except that you seek nearness to Allah, Exalted is He, through what brings you closer to Him of righteous deeds. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said this.

The fourth: except that you love me as you love your kin. Ibn Zayd said this.

The fifth: except that you love your kin and maintain your ties of kinship. Al-Mawardi related this. The first is the most sound.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 42, verses 32–36:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among His signs are the ships sailing through the sea﴾. By "al-jawar" (the ships) is meant the ships. Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Abu 'Amr read "al-jawari" with a yā' when connected (in continuous recitation). However, Ibn Kathir also pauses with a yā', while Abu 'Amr pauses without a yā'. Ya'qub agrees with Ibn Kathir, and the rest read without a yā' both in connection and in pause. Abu 'Ali said: the analogical form (al-qiyas) is what Ibn Kathir followed, and whoever omits it, the omission of the like of this is frequent in their speech.

﴿Like mountains﴾. Ibn Qutaybah said: like mountains, its singular being 'alam (a landmark, a high mountain). It is narrated from al-Khalil ibn Ahmad that he said: everything that is elevated, according to the Arabs, is an 'alam.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If He wills, He stills the wind﴾ which drives them, ﴿so they remain motionless upon its surface﴾, meaning the ships (al-jawari), ﴿motionless upon the back of the sea﴾, that is, still upon the surface of the sea [not running].

﴿Or He destroys them﴾, that is, He causes them to perish and drowns them, and the intended ones are the people of the ships. Therefore He said: ﴿for what they have earned﴾, that is, of sins, ﴿and He pardons much﴾ of their sins, so He saves them from destruction.

﴿And that those who dispute concerning Our signs may know﴾. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read "wa-ya'lama" with a raised vowel (ḍamma), as a resumption (isti'naf) and cut off from the first; the rest read it in the accusative (naṣb). Al-Farra' said: it is subordinated to the jussive (jazm), except that it has been diverted, and when the jussive is diverted from what it is conjoined to, it takes the accusative.

The exegetes have two opinions concerning the meaning of the verse.

(p-290) One of them: "and those who dispute concerning the signs of God will know, when they are seized by drowning, that there is no refuge for them."

The second: that after the Resurrection they will know that there is no escape for them from the punishment.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So whatever you have been given of a thing﴾, that is, whatever you have been given of the world, it is a provision you enjoy, then it passes away swiftly, ﴿but what is with God is better and more lasting for those who believe﴾, not for the disbelievers, because He has prepared for them in the Hereafter the punishment.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 42, verses 37–43:**

God's words: ﴿Those who avoid the grave sins and indecencies﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "kabira al-ithm" (كَبِيرَ الإثْمِ) in the singular, without an alif, while the rest read it with an alif (كَبائِرَ الإثْمِ). We have explained the major sins (kaba'ir) in the commentary on Surah an-Nisa' [4:31]. Regarding the meaning of "al-fawahish" (الفَواحِشِ) here, there are two opinions. The first is fornication (al-zina). The second is the offences that entail prescribed penalties (hudud).

God's words: ﴿And when they are angry, they forgive﴾, meaning they pardon those who wronged them, seeking the reward of God, exalted is He.

﴿And those who respond to their Lord﴾, meaning they answer Him in what He calls them to.

﴿And their affair is by consultation among themselves﴾. Ibn Qutaybah said: meaning they consult with one another about it. al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that they do not act on an opinion alone until they agree upon it together.

God's words: ﴿And those who, when wrong is inflicted on them, defend themselves﴾. The scholars differed concerning this "wrong" (al-baghy) in three opinions.

The first: it is the transgression of the disbelievers against the Muslims. 'Ata' said: they are the believers whom the disbelievers drove out of Makkah and transgressed against, then God empowered them over them, and they defended themselves. Zayd ibn Aslam said: the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ were in Makkah in two groups. One group was harmed and would pardon the polytheists, and the other group was harmed and would defend itself. God, mighty and majestic, praised them all. He said of those who did not defend themselves: ﴿And when they are angry, they forgive﴾, and He said of those who defended themselves: ﴿And those who, when wrong is inflicted on them, defend themselves﴾, meaning against the polytheists. Ibn Zayd said: He mentioned the Emigrants (muhajirun), who were of two kinds: a kind that pardoned, and a kind that defended itself. He said: ﴿And when they are angry, they forgive﴾, and He began with them. Of those who defended themselves He said: ﴿And those who, when wrong is inflicted on them, defend themselves﴾, meaning against the polytheists. And He said: ﴿And those who respond to their Lord﴾ up to His words: ﴿and spend﴾, and these are the Helpers (al-Ansar). Then He mentioned the third kind and said: ﴿And those who, when wrong is inflicted on them, defend themselves﴾, against the polytheists.

The second: it is the transgression of Muslims against Muslims specifically.

The third: it is general to all transgressors, whether they are Muslims or disbelievers.

Section

Scholars of abrogation (naskh, the cancelling of a ruling by a later one) differed concerning this verse. God's words: ﴿But We have made it﴾. Concerning the pronoun in "made it" there are two views. The first: it refers to the Qur'an. The second: it refers to faith.

﴿a light (nur)﴾, that is, a radiance and a guide to the Oneness of God, ﴿by which We guide whomever We will﴾ [of Our servants] to the religion of truth.

﴿And you are surely guiding﴾, that is, you are calling ﴿to a straight path﴾, which is Islam.
